title: Pumpkin: modeled ₹366/qtl left, Kathua → Bhuntar
summary: January 2021: reported pumpkin prices at Kathua and Bhuntar imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 96% of 25 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹366 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 194 same-variety market pairs screened for pumpkin in January 2021; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Bhuntar report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: January 2021
scenes.caption: Kathua (Jammu and Kashmir) and Bhuntar (Himachal Pradesh) both reported pumpkin prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 25 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Kathua reported a median ₹1,450 per quintal. Bhuntar reported a median ₹2,100 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹600/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹600 per quintal, and Bhuntar was dearer on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 412 km by road
scenes.caption: 412 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~7 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹89/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹338 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹220 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Bhuntar report, the rule selects 21 of 23 modeled shipping days. 20 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹366 per quintal (₹241 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Pumpkin route from Kathua to Bhuntar was positive on 96% of matched days in January 2021. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹36,600, or ₹24,100 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

title: Pumpkin: modeled ₹253/qtl left, Palayam → Chala
summary: November 2021: reported pumpkin prices at Palayam and Chala imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 100% of 24 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹253 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 362 same-variety market pairs screened for pumpkin in November 2021; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Chala report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: November 2021
scenes.caption: Palayam (Kerala) and Chala (Kerala) both reported pumpkin prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 24 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Palayam reported a median ₹1,000 per quintal. Chala reported a median ₹1,526 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹526/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹526 per quintal, and Chala was dearer on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 380 km by road
scenes.caption: 380 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~7 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹82/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹285 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹178 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Chala report, the rule selects 24 of 24 modeled shipping days. 24 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹253 per quintal (₹156 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Pumpkin route from Palayam to Chala was positive on 100% of matched days in November 2021. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹25,300, or ₹15,600 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to pumpkin
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹82/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Pumpkin route from Palayam to Chala was positive on 100% of matched days in November 2021. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹25,300, or ₹15,600 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.
